clue.text: Spoke to artist's face

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; the 's is a link
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a painter directly, to their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past tense of speak, but it is a noun: a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a line or bar running out from a centre, as a spoke does on a wheel.

clue.text: Where to treat oil? Engineers find it hot round the Pole

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the word for hot goes round the Pole, enclosing it

parts.note: fiery means burning hot
N, the North Pole

explanation.surface: Engineers working near the Arctic find their oil plant is surprisingly hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts N inside FIERY after its first two letters, making FINERY; 'find it' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is the plant where crude oil is processed into fuels, so it is where oil is treated.

clue.text: River mud -don't disturb — go from here by canal

indicators.note: disturbing the letters stirs them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A notice by a muddy river asks people not to stir up the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of R, MUD and DONT gives the German city; the Dortmund-Ems Canal starts there.
explanation.definitionFit: Dortmund is a German city at the head of the Dortmund-Ems Canal, a place you can set off from by water.

clue.text: Remains of wood deposit on land

parts.note: ash is what is left when wood burns
ore is a mineral deposit

explanation.surface: Burnt timber leaves a residue on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or towards dry land rather than at sea.

clue.text: At a distance reaper sounds ridiculous

indicators.note: says the pair of words is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: at a distance is FAR, and a reaper is a SICKLE, the curved harvesting blade

explanation.surface: The Grim Reaper, heard from afar, sounds absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: FAR SICKLE said aloud gives the answer; 'reaper' is the tool, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical describes something so absurd it resembles a farce, which is to say ridiculous.

clue.text: Unable to wait for a giant

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, one of the pair Gog and Magog in the Guildhall, London

explanation.surface: Someone cannot wait for a giant to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited, too impatient for what is coming to wait calmly.

clue.text: Class of animal with energy and a lot of blood?

parts.note: a cat is an animal
E is the physics symbol for energy
gory means covered in much blood

explanation.surface: A zoologist asks which grouping fits a bloody-minded beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or division of things sharing some quality.

clue.text: Container right for opening of hot spot

parts.note: a crate is a box for carrying goods

explanation.surface: A box is chosen because it suits the start of a heated spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is the mouth of a volcano, the opening at a place of great heat.

clue.text: Left a match after everything else

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A cricketer leaves a match once everything else is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest comes last in time, arriving after every other thing.

clue.text: Largely away from home -gin time, and some return

parts.note: forth means out and away, as in setting forth from home

indicators.note: the run of gin, time and some is read backwards as a whole

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mostly away travelling drinks gin at times and brings some home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'Largely' looks like an adverb on the trip, but it is the whole definition; 'return' reverses gin, time and some as one run, not each word apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning mostly or in the main, the same as largely.

clue.text: See 9
Boat in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a pan with a perforated insert for cooking food in steam

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a steam-driven ship and a covered cooking pan used to steam vegetables.

clue.text: Near mute, possibly, but able to count

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A child who is nearly silent may still be good at sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerate means competent with numbers, the arithmetic counterpart of literate.

clue.text: Exit black girl, having lost head

indicators.note: its first letter is dropped from the word for black girl

parts.note: an old term, now offensive, for a black woman

explanation.surface: A girl leaves the scene after losing her head.
explanation.walkthrough: The dated term for the girl loses its first letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of going out, which is an exit.

clue.text: Aesthetically pleasing English by walker and worker

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An English rambler and a labourer stroll beautifully together.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes graceful, stylish design that pleases the eye.

clue.text: Complaint of wrong treatment in lip

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the lip word

parts.note: the rim is the lip of a cup or bowl

indicators.note: the letters receive treatment, being worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient grumbles about the wrong care given to a sore lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grumble, but it is an illness; 'treatment' is the anagram signal for wrong, and 'in' puts the result inside the lip word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection, and a complaint is an ailment in the medical sense.

clue.text: Largely arranged for exhibition hall

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The exhibits were mostly organised for the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery is a room or building where art is put on display.

clue.text: Request for reliable groups of sailors, say, on fun voyage

parts.note: a plea is an urgent request
sure means dependable

indicators.note: say tells us the word for sailors is heard, not spelt

parts.note: crews are the teams who man ships

explanation.surface: Someone asks for trustworthy sailors to staff a holiday trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure cruise is a sea trip taken for enjoyment rather than transport.

clue.text: Very large adverse balance in fossil fuel

indicators.note: the deficit word goes inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
a loss is an account balance in the red

explanation.surface: Fossil fuel firms post an enormous deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means gigantic, as huge as the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Envoy, tired, losing head over girl

indicators.note: the shortened word for tired lies over the girl, wrapping round her
the first letter of the word for tired goes

parts.note: weary means tired
Miss is a title for a young woman

explanation.surface: A worn-out diplomat loses his head over a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: WEARY loses its head to give EARY, and 'over' covers MISS with it: E-MISS-ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a representative sent on a mission, the same as an envoy.

clue.text: Largely regrettable reaction

indicators.note: something regrettable is bad or wrong, so the letters are put wrongly

explanation.surface: Most of the response was unfortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the immune system's reaction to a harmless substance.

clue.text: See 15
Setter's left to take in significance

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves; setter's means setter is, I'M
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker has gone off to absorb the meaning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' is a second hint at the word's verb sense of bringing goods into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Import as a noun means meaning or importance, as in a matter of great import.

clue.text: Journalist tired out without love

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the zero
out means put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A weary reporter is left with no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TIRED to EDITR, which goes 'without' (around) O.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a journalist who prepares and oversees what is published.

clue.text: See 17
Report of one who interferes with fruit

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a meddler is a busybody who interferes

explanation.surface: A busybody is reported to have tampered with the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small brown fruit eaten once it has softened and begun to rot.

clue.text: Nero turning to rodent, largely-very large

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: The emperor Nero is transformed into a huge rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges NERO to ENOR; MOUSE 'largely' loses its last letter to give MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means vastly big, exactly the sense of very large.

clue.text: Man, say, is left without feet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means the letters for feet are removed

explanation.surface: A man is left with no feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is in the Irish Sea; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of an island of this kind.

clue.text: Explosive utterance attributed to Brutus

indicators.note: the letters are assigned new places, a loose sign that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent remark is credited to Caesar's assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden violent expression of feeling, an explosive utterance.

clue.text: Take from the easiest and leave the rest

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Advice to grab the easy pickings and ignore everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave the rest' reads as 'ignore the remainder', but 'rest' is the definition; 'leave the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a rest taken in hot countries.

clue.text: Writer's venture formed with good in it

definitions.note: writer's here stands for writer is

indicators.note: the G goes inside the rearranged word
formed means shaped into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author's business project is set up with something worthwhile inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' is the anagram signal for venture, and 'in it' puts the G inside the result; Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Largely no good, otherwise in fact

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently

parts.note: G is short for good; no says it is dropped

explanation.surface: Mostly worthless, but in other respects actually fine.
explanation.walkthrough: LARGELY without G (no good) leaves LARELY, rearranged 'otherwise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Really means actually, as a matter of real fact.
